newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Eyes on digital prize at BSkyB.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Eyes on digital prize at BSkyB.

text.p: Satellite broadcaster BSkyB is poised to unveil interim profit growth of around 25 percent on Wednesday but share analysts said all eyes are on the company's expansion into digital services.
Pre-tax profit for the six months to December 31 is forecast to total between 131.1 million and 138 million pounds, against 106.3 million at the halfway point a year ago.

BSkyB's first quarter profit rose 31 percent to 66 million pounds as its total paying subscribers increased to 5.65 million. Further growth is expected in this second quarter, which includes the busy Christmas period.
But attention is increasingly focused on BSkyB's plan to launch digital satellite services into the UK in late 1997.
A newspaper report this week said that a BSkyB board meeting on Tuesday was expected to give formal backing for the launch.

BSkyB is expected to place an order for a million digital decoders with manufacturers, at an estimated cost of some 250 million pounds. A decoder will be required to receive the 200 or satellite channels.
BSkyB has also joined forces with ITV companies Carlton Communications and Granada Group to apply for digital terrestrial licences in the UK.

BSkyB is involved in digital television in Germany as a partner of Kirch Group in the DF1 network. But DF1, launched amid great fanfare in July, has struggled and is reported to have only 20,000 subscribers.
